title.narrative: Multilateral M&D and NSD Support to PRC via IFRC

description.narrative:
As of April 2024, Poland has recorded a total of 19.8 million border crossing from Ukraine and is hosting around 956,000 individual refugees. While recent surveys indicate that most refugees from Ukraine hope to return to their place of origin, the majority are planning to stay in Poland for the time being because of ongoing instability and concerns for their security in Ukraine. As the emergency evolves into a protracted stage, those who remain in Poland are facing challenges extending beyond immediate basic needs to encompass socio-economic integration and comprehensive protection. Among Poland’s current refugee population, a significant number of individuals and groups, e.g. households composed of women, children, and older persons, with family separation, face heightened protection needs and increased risks of abuse, exploitation, and gender-based violence.
Through BRC's scoping visit in August 2023 and various partnership meetings, a comprehensive approach to supporting PRC and vulnerable populations is recognised as crucial. This is a two-year multilateral partnership with IFRC (and in turn the Polish Red Cross, PRC) to support people displaced by the Ukraine Crisis in Poland and other vulnerable groups of people on the move, as well as vulnerable population in Poland, who have also been significantly impacted by the Ukraine crisis. This grant also aims to support PRC’s National Society Development objectives, to build PRC capacity and to increase the relevance and quality of humanitarian assistance provided by PRC to affected populations.
First payment for multilateral M&D and NSD support to PRC via IFRC
